adjudication.evidence: P1 (460–475) shows a sustained offset in N/E/U with return-like behavior: large negative U (~-7.3) and positive N (~+5.9), followed by recovery toward pre-offset levels by index ~480; interior points (e.g., 468–474) remain offset, supporting a genuine temporary platform. P2 (501–503) is a 3-point spike without sustained shift or return—N/E/U jump abruptly but no persistent offset; also coincides with missing index 500 and 519, and numerical tool evidence identifies best pulse at 505–506, not 501–503. P3 (505) is a single point outlier (N~31.7, E~12.7) inconsistent with surrounding motion and lacks return; likely noise or artifact. Only P1 satisfies criteria for genuine temporary offset: sustained shift + opposing return across axes, interior consistency, and physical plausibility.
